## Address conventions and validation boundary

Source-only reconnaissance, 2026-10-09; no build or ROM read was performed. Source paths are relative to `tomatotrans-1.1.1/`. Confidence definitions are in [translation_project_overview.md](translation_project_overview.md). “Confirmed” in the inventories confirms what the source explicitly declares/targets, not that a binary has matching contents or that gameplay semantics were tested.

- **ROM bus address**: the CPU-visible cartridge address used by `.org`, literals and calls, e.g. `0x0862C250`.
- **ROM file offset**: zero-based seek position, e.g. `0x0062C250`. For this toolkit's `0x08000000` mapping, `bus = offset + 0x08000000`; reverse conversion subtracts that base. C++ instead clears/sets bit `0x08000000`, which assumes this particular ROM window. Do not apply its mask blindly to RAM or other cartridge windows.
- **RAM/VRAM/I/O bus address**: `0x02...` EWRAM, `0x03...` IWRAM, `0x04...` registers, `0x05...` palette RAM, `0x06...` VRAM. These have no ROM file offset. Some numerically similar operands are transfer flags rather than addresses.
- A Thumb function pointer may have bit 0 set. The pointer is then `entry + 1`; remove that bit before deriving the instruction offset. Table pointers and unaligned script pointer locations must not be rounded automatically.

Original-Japanese locations remain the addressing basis for assembly patches. A patch site at an original address may contain replacement code in the output. Fixed translated tables and dynamic pool allocations are translation-only; `.autoregion` placements are build-dependent and unresolved here. The existing English ROM and BPS patch were not compared to these sources.

## Allocation ownership

Ranges are half-open unless stated otherwise.

| Bus range | File offset range | Owner/purpose | Evidence | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0864B4EC`–`0x087F0000` | `0x0064B4EC`–`0x007F0000` | Assumed translation text/image pool; capacity `0x1A4B14` bytes. This is an allocation assumption, not a verified free-space scan. | `inserter/ta_insert.cpp:8-9,27`; sequential `InsertString` and image `nextPos` writes. | Confirmed boundaries; Candidate safe free space |
| `0x087F0000`–`0x087F1BE0` | `0x007F0000`–`0x007F1BE0` | Reserved translated fixed text tables. | `asm/addresses.inc:2-11`; menu `RESTRUCT` and `BLOCKSTART`. | Confirmed source allocation |
| Existing code/data `.region` ranges | Bus minus `0x08000000` | Replacement routines and reusable slack for `.autoregion` helpers/sprite data. Not a separate guaranteed free-space block. | Assembly `.region`, `.area`, `.autoregion` occurrences in ledger. | Confirmed declarations; Unconfirmed final helper placements |
| `0x02038000`–`0x02038060` | N/A | Translation scratch EWRAM; upstream comments only say the game “doesn't seem” to use all WRAM. | `asm/addresses.inc:13-20`. | Confirmed aliases; Candidate collision-free lifetime |

`TOMATO_SIZE` is a reporting ceiling for the pool, **not** the final ROM size. The fixed tables lie beyond it. Neither the actual input size nor the high-water mark of the translated output was measured. Do not allocate new mod data at either pool base, at `0x087F1BE0`, or in reclaimed code slack until ownership and build output are verified. String deduplication may point into fixed tables, so relocated text is not necessarily confined to the growing pool.

| BattleAilmentsText | `0x087F17DE` | `0x007F17DE` | `0x60` | Four 24-byte suffixes; original `0x08632E14`, stride 8. |

There is a two-byte gap between the NamingScreenText reservation and DefaultNamesText. Menu UI names/descriptions can also be independently relocated through BLOCKFIXED; the fixed battle tables are not the only translated text copies.

All ranges here are half-open. The literal contents, full loader continuation, other record consumers and gameplay fields require ROM inspection/disassembly. The source establishes one graphics-pointer write site, but no difficulty pair, power byte, special-effect flag or Kaizo threshold has been promoted to a confirmed gameplay field. Non-text record bytes are not all guaranteed unchanged: the Choo-Choo image relocation is a concrete exception.

## Legacy script-layout leads

`hacking notes.txt` predates the current patches and contains uncertainty and typos. Its address inventory below is **Candidate** evidence only. Useful leads: bus `0x0862D3E4` (file `0x0062D3E4`) “super blocks,” possible stride `0x1C`; subordinate `0x10`-byte records with text pointer at `+0xA` and line ID at `+0xE`; bus `0x08100E75` example event stream, referenced by `0x08140330` and `0x0862D414`. These may be distinct layers, not one universal script schema.

The notes trace opcode argument selection through `0x080223E6`–`0x0802245E`, copier `0x0802F97C`, and argument-length tables `0x0862B6C4`, `0x0862B815`, `0x0862B736`. Tentative pointer-bearing FD/FE opcodes include `FD 35/36`, `FE 07`, `FE C8/C9/D2/7A`. Verify opcode lengths before scanning for event pointers. The malformed range `862C090-8062C21A` is retained as uncertain text, not accepted as an address range.

## Address inventory method

The following appendices preserve source locations and operands rather than infer all targets are functions. Assembly literals, origins, boundaries, comments and calls; inserter offsets; menu address parameters; battle text pointer locations; dump headers; and pointer manifests are inventoried. Hex lengths, IDs, masks and bytecodes are excluded or explicitly called out. Arithmetic operands retain their source expressions; a literal base is not the full computed target. Script pointer lists enumerate pointer slots, not pointed-to string addresses. Generated tables are source evidence, not an output ROM map.

## Appendix A: Assembly address occurrences

Each row retains the actual operand and nearest preceding comment. Explicit origins, region boundaries, named aliases, and call operands are Confirmed source references; their game purposes remain Probable or Candidate. Comment-only references are Candidate. Expressions may add/subtract offsets from the displayed base; conditional branches are not claimed to execute in every build. The ledger includes hardware operands to prevent accidental treatment as ROM offsets.

Generic image pixel indices, codec masks and count constants are not ROM addresses.

## Appendix D: Main dialogue pointer slot catalogue

`pointers1.dat` physical row 1 corresponds to dialogue ID `000`; `InsertMainScript` indexes rows in message order, ignoring the written ID value. Each listed **file offset** is a 32-bit pointer slot overwritten with the translated message bus address. `FFFFFFFF` is a sentinel, not an address. Slots are often unaligned. The full row is retained so each discovered slot has a source, purpose and confidence. The numeric slot inventory is Confirmed source data; its correctness for a ROM revision is unverified.

To convert **each** offset below to a ROM bus address, add `0x08000000`; e.g. `000F9A9D` is bus `0x080F9A9D`. These are not the original message payload addresses.
